answer: One agent runs one trellis bay, mounts a velvet panel, and posts an 80-credit bond; one bay per key in the registry. Each epoch the agent files a plume deposit log with wind run and particle count. An auditor recomputes the expected deposit from the published plume-dispersion table for that bay and burns the bond on a mismatch or a reused log. The k-th panel costs 30+5(k-1), so 1,000 fake bays cost 2,527,500 in fees plus 80,000 bonded. A rented-filter ring fails: one panel cannot show distinct deposits across bays. An honest bay pays 30 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
